notes: Summary: POC completed (Nov 2025). Argosy evaluated Redwood Private vs incumbent (Velvet HealthML) for structured report generation and EHR tool-calls.

Key callouts: Redwood performed well on throughput and latency in Dedicated tests, cost profile attractive. HOWEVER: repeated quality regressions in structured output mapping and tool-calling reliability compared to incumbent.

POC details: 3-week sandbox mimicking discharge-summary pipeline; used a pinned open model + Redwood runtime quantization profile. Failures observed: malformed JSON outputs, missing required EHR fields, function-calls returning inconsistent parameter schemas (function name mapped but params null).

Quote from Dir. of Clinical Informatics: 'We need deterministic structured outputs that map 1:1 to our EHR schema — Velvet's connector produced cleaner JSON 9/10; Redwood hit that 6/10 and we can't risk errors in patient data.'

Security: Argosy required BAA + HSM/KMS integration and per-field audit logs. Security team flagged gaps in drive-by artifacts; requested encryption at-rest with customer-managed keys for on-prem deployment. Long approval timeline (legal + infosec).

Commercial dynamics: Velvet offered an integration bundle (connector + tuning) and aggressive pricing for 18-month contract. Argosy prioritized reducing vetting effort — incumbent already had a reference customer in regional hospital network which reduced perceived risk.

Suggested remediation if re-opened: produce deterministic structured-output bench with their sample dataset, commit to a short targeted engineering spike to fix function-calling schema regressions, provide signed BAA + customer-managed key reference architecture, and offer a short pilot with warranty on schema correctness.
